newsitem.title: TURKEY: Jealous Turkish brothers kill 10 to save "honour".
newsitem.headline: Jealous Turkish brothers kill 10 to save "honour".

text.p: Two jealous Turkish brothers sprayed a house with bullets on Sunday, murdering their wives and eight other people in an "honour killing" amid a web of complex family ties.
"Ten people, among them two children and five women, were shot dead," a local police commissioner told Reuters.
State-run Anatolian news agency said the killers were two brothers who attacked their mother-in-law's house in Istanbul's rundown Esenler district at 4 a.m. (0100 GMT).
The pair believed their wives Nuran and Aycan Aydin, both sisters, were drinking alcohol with two other brothers from another family inside, it said.

The mother-in-law, the wives, their two male friends and the five-year-old daughter of one of the killers were among those who died in a hail of bullets. Four people unrelated to any of the families were also killed.
Police said the killers fired dozens of shots from a Kalashnikov assault rifle and a 9 mm pistol. ATV television station showed pictures of bloodstains on upturned beds in the house.
Interior walls were pockmarked with dozens of bullet holes and splashed with blood.

"The killing appears likely to have been caused by a matter of honour," Anatolian said. "Honour killings", in which males kill female relatives for keeping male company deemed unsuitable, are common in Turkey.
Anatolian said one of the suspected killers, Celal Aydin, was arrested near the house later in the day. Police were searching for his brother Abdullah, it said.
